title: Connections on the go
summary: Choose the right connection for the task.

passages.heading: The core idea
passages.markdown: A connector’s shape is only one part of a connection. USB-C describes a reversible physical connector; the device, port, and cable still determine supported data speed, charging, and video features. A cable that charges a laptop may not support an external display. Read the specifications at both ends and check the cable rating before promising that one lead will handle everything on a desk.

passages.heading: In the real world
passages.markdown: Bluetooth is useful for nearby peripherals such as headsets and keyboards. Pairing establishes a trusted relationship between devices, while NFC typically exchanges small amounts of information at very short range. A mobile hotspot shares an upstream cellular connection with other devices and can consume a data allowance quickly. Docks consolidate desk connections, but features depend on the host interface and dock capabilities. Test video, networking, charging, and peripherals separately when investigating a dock issue.

passages.heading: Make it stick
passages.markdown: Put it into practice by explaining the decision in your own words. In a support scenario, identify the requirement first, connect it to the relevant technology, and check the result against that requirement. If the evidence changes, revisit your reasoning rather than repeating the same action. Document what you observed so the next person can understand your conclusion.
